x: After one lap he was still in the twenties and although he began to make ground on the second circuit it was a slow and painful business against such opposition as Adcocks and Kilby (Coventry), Rose, Wheeler and Wyatt (New Zealand), Tulloh, Roberts and Barlow.
He just failed to make the final of the 100 metres and then with an excellent jump of 22'-7¾" had to give best by ¾" to Rose (QPH) in the long jump.

Gerard ran steadily throughout the race near the front of the pack but when Brendan Foster opened up with 600 metres to go, stringing out Rose and Spedding behind him, it seemed that the Irishman had no hope of a medal.
